So there is nothing here that a person using the product, or a manual tester, can run into. The product already stops them and tells them what to do.
What is left is a back-end tidiness issue only.

If the invoice request is sent straight to the back end for a work order with no contact — skipping the screen that would have stopped you — the back end answers with a general "something went wrong" server error instead of a clear message saying a contact is missing. Nobody can reach that by clicking the product.
The original ticket also blamed the wrong thing.

It implied the pre-set job ("canned line") chosen for the work order mattered. It does not. Eleven different pre-set jobs, covering every way they can be priced, all behaved identically. The only thing that matters is whether a contact is set.

All three are the same pattern — a missing or unresolvable prerequisite producing a 500 instead of a validation message.
25 work orders were created during this re-test, each tagged
in its tech story, and all were deleted and verified absent afterwards. One asset (

— its only contact — because the product's confirmation for choosing a contact writes it to the asset. That is recorded rather than reverted, since reverting would require clearing a field the product marks as required.
Where this expected behaviour comes from: nothing written down. Stating that plainly rather than dressing it up.

We checked the six report specifications and the stories under this epic, and none of them says what answer the system should give when an invoice is requested for a work order that has no contact set. The expectation in this ticket rests on consistency with the answers the product already gives for other missing prerequisites — for example "Work order is not complete." and "Line can`t be completed with unfulfilled part requests." — and on the general principle that a missing piece of required information should produce a clear rejection rather than a server error. That is a reasonable expectation, but it is our reading and not a quoted requirement.
This ticket is already closed. It is recorded here so that the record is honest about what the expectation rested on.
